item.title: Forced out, assaulted, unpaid: Teachers remain under pressure
item.description:
A university vice-chancellor was allegedly forced to sign a resignation letter inside his office. A college principal was prevented from entering his institution. Teachers were pushed and assaulted amid demands for their removal.
More than two years after forced resignations and attacks on teachers emerged as a major concern across educational institutions, fresh incidents suggest the problem is far from over, despite repeated government directives intended to protect affected teachers and restore their jobs and salaries.
The Alliance of Deprived Institution Heads and Teachers estimates that around 4,500 teachers and heads of institutions have been affected since 2024.
It claims at least eight teachers died following physical or psychological trauma, more than 500 were injured or fell ill, and over 1,000 are still not receiving salaries or allowances.
The figures could not be independently verified.
The latest incident occurred at Rajshahi Medical University on Tuesday, when Vice-Chancellor Prof Dr Md Jawadul Haque was allegedly forced to sign a resignation letter after a group entered his office while he was attending a virtual meeting with Health Ministry officials.
His personal secretary and section officer Nazmul Hossain was allegedly assaulted when he intervened and was also forced to sign a resignation letter.
Nazmul later filed a case with Rajpara Police Station. Police arrested Abdus Salam, 56, in connection with the incident.
Police initially said Salam’s political affiliation had not been confirmed.
Rajpara Thana BNP President Mizanur Rahman, however, told media that Salam was a vice-president of the thana BNP unit and had been present during the incident.
The RMU incident came less than two weeks after tensions at Mohammadpur Central College, where teachers alleged that students and outsiders obstructed Principal Lt Col (retd) Md Shahidul Hasan and harassed teachers.
On September 24, some students and outsiders allegedly locked the administrative building gate and demanded the principal’s removal amid tensions surrounding a Class XI orientation program.
Bangla lecturer Shawon Ahmed Kabir was allegedly pushed while trying to calm the situation, while teacher representative Dr Mohammad Shamsul Alam was also allegedly assaulted.
Teachers later submitted a written complaint seeking action, and the college governing body assured them that the allegations would be investigated.
Bangladesh Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal subsequently expelled two members over allegations linked to the incident.
Teacher representatives say such incidents form part of a much broader problem dating back to the political upheaval of 2024.
Alliance convener Anwarul Islam Talukder said more than 1,000 affected teachers were still not receiving salaries or allowances, while many had been unable to return to their institutions for more than a year.
“We have repeatedly approached the Education Ministry and the Secondary and Higher Education Division, but there has been little progress,” he told Dhaka Tribune.
The government has issued a series of directives since reports of forced resignations began emerging.
The Education Ministry said in September 2024 that forcing teachers to resign was unacceptable.
Further instructions followed concerning salaries and allowances, reinstatement and action against institutions that failed to comply.
Teacher representatives, however, say implementation remains incomplete.
Anwarul Islam, principal of Suapur Nannar School and College in Dhamrai, said he was among those forced from office after August 2024.
He alleged that a group of teachers and students accused him of irregularities on August 11 and demanded his resignation.
The following day, he said, around 15 people went to his Mirpur residence and forced him to sign a resignation letter.
Former Dhaka City College principal and alliance president Md Bedar Uddin Ahmed said the organization had repeatedly submitted complaints and memorandums to government offices.
“Despite government directives, many teachers are still unable to return to their workplaces,” he said.
Teachers from other institutions, including Viqarunnisa Noon School and College, have also previously alleged that they were forced to resign following the events of August 2024.
Acting principal Keka Roy and assistant professor Dr Farhana Khanam were among those who made such allegations.
The issue is now set to receive international scrutiny.
UN Special Rapporteur on the right to education Farida Shaheed is scheduled to visit Bangladesh from November 23 to December 4, according to information provided by the teachers’ alliance and reported by media.
The group says she will examine allegations involving teachers and students who faced mob attacks at educational institutions after August 5, 2024, with the Unesco Dhaka office assisting during the visit.
The alliance said affected teachers have submitted complaints and supporting materials for the process, including information on their employment status, cases, photographs, videos and audio recordings.
The exact number of complaints submitted has not been established.
Educationist Rasheda K Chowdhury said attacks and harassment of teachers, alongside disputes over salaries, allowances and professional dignity, reflected a broader crisis of confidence in the education system.
“If we want quality education, we need quality teachers,” she said, stressing the importance of both investment in and respect for the profession.
Prof Mohammad Mujibur Rahman of Dhaka University’s Institute of Education and Research said allegations against teachers should be investigated through due process, with teachers given an opportunity to respond before decisions are taken.
“Firstly, teachers need to act independently. Again, our perspective has yet to evolve. As a nation, we still fail to recognize the importance of education and those who teach,” he told Dhaka Tribune.
Educationists stressed that complaints against teachers or disputes over institutional decisions should not be ignored.
Allegations of misconduct or irregularities should be investigated and, where substantiated, acted upon.
But they said those processes should take place through established institutional and legal procedures, rather than physical intimidation, humiliation or forcing teachers to sign resignation letters.

item.title: 17-year-old Rakibul abducted for ransom, killed by friend
item.description:
Seventeen-year-old Md Rakibul Islam came to Dhaka after his HSC exams, hoping to prepare for university admission, but was allegedly abducted for ransom and later killed, police said.
Rakib was staying at a mess in East Shewrapara and attending a coaching centre in Farmgate. On September 16, he was called outside through a WhatsApp call but never returned.
According to police, Rakib became acquainted online with Abdullah Al Mamun alias Mamun Sarker, 24, shortly after arriving in Dhaka. Mamun allegedly called him to the area in front of Shewrapara Metro Rail Station on September 16 and took him to his home in Sukrabad.
Police said Mamun held Rakib hostage and demanded Tk15 lakh from his family. During a struggle, he allegedly twisted Rakib’s neck, causing his death.
Mamun then placed the body in a carton, sealed it with Scotch tape and took it by autorickshaw to Gabtoli bus terminal. He later travelled to Dimla in Nilphamari and buried the carton containing Rakib’s body in a pit in a betel nut orchard in front of his home on September 17, police said. DMP Crime Prevention (North) Joint Commissioner Md Mahidul Islam disclosed the details at a press briefing at the DMP Media Centre on Wednesday.
Police said the family paid Tk4 lakh through four bKash and three Nagad numbers after receiving ransom demands and threats to kill Rakib.
Rakib’s elder brother, Johurul Islam Jibon, initially filed a general diary with Kafrul Police Station and later filed a case over the abduction and ransom demand.
Mahidul said police traced Mamun as the user of two WhatsApp numbers used to demand the ransom. He was arrested from the Sukrabad bus stand area in Sher-e-Bangla Nagar on October 5.
During interrogation, Mamun reportedly confessed to taking Rakib to his home to collect the ransom and said Rakib died when he twisted his neck during a struggle.
Police recovered Rakib’s body from the spot indicated by Mamun in Dimla on Tuesday with the assistance of local police. His elder brother later identified the body.
The body was sent to Nilphamari Modern Sadar Hospital for autopsy.
Police also recovered Tk50,000 in cash, allegedly from the ransom money, from Mamun.
Mahidul said the investigation is underway to determine whether anyone else was involved and to examine the ransom transactions and other aspects of the case.

item.title: Ansar-VDP begins advance security measures for Durga Puja
item.description:
The Bangladesh Ansar and Village Defense Party (VDP) has begun advance security measures across the country to ensure the upcoming Sharodiya Durga Puja is celebrated safely and peacefully.
As part of the preparations, Ansar-VDP members are visiting idol-making sites, puja mandaps and temples, according to a press release issued on Wednesday.
The release said Ansar-VDP members at the field level are exchanging views with leaders of puja celebration committees, temple authorities and people involved in making idols.
The discussions cover idol security, the law and order situation during the puja, and the duties and responsibilities of puja celebration committees and Ansar-VDP members.
The activities are being carried out at district and upazila levels under the directive of Major General Abdul Motaleb Sajjad Mahmud, director general of the Bangladesh Ansar and Village Defense Party.
Allowance-receiving (stipendiary) Ansar-VDP members are working in the field under the supervision of upazila Ansar-VDP officers and instructors.
During the visits, those concerned are being advised to remain vigilant about the security of puja mandaps, entry and exit management, lighting arrangements and fire safety.
Emphasis is also being placed on coordination with local administration and law enforcement agencies to avoid any undesirable situation.
In addition, puja celebration committees have been requested to arrange accommodation and necessary facilities for Ansar members who will be on duty during the puja.
They have also been asked to cooperate in maintaining overall security and discipline at puja mandaps and in taking swift, coordinated action during emergencies.
The release further stated that Ansar-VDP members are being kept ready to perform duties at various puja mandaps across the country to ensure public safety and maintain law and order during the Sharodiya Durga Puja.
Through coordination with the local administration, law enforcement agencies and puja celebration committees, the advance preparations and field-level activities will continue to ensure a safe and peaceful puja.

item.title: Heading to Bangladesh? Dengue vaccine now an option in Australia
item.description:
As Bangladesh grapples with widespread dengue, the availability of a dengue vaccine in Australia has brought a new preventive option for Bangladeshi expatriates worried about travelling home with their families.
Qdenga, a vaccine designed to protect against dengue disease, has become available in Australia following approval by the Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA), with the Australian Technical Advisory Group on Immunisation (ATAGI) issuing clinical advice on its use in September.
The development is particularly significant for Bangladeshis living in Australia, many of whom regularly travel home with their children and other family members and have become increasingly concerned about dengue infections and deaths in Bangladesh.
Qdenga is approved in Australia for people aged four years and above.
However, health authorities do not recommend that every traveller automatically receive it.
ATAGI particularly recommends Qdenga for eligible people who have previously had dengue and are at risk of future exposure.
For people aged four and above who have never had dengue and are undertaking short-term travel, vaccination can be considered following an individual risk-benefit assessment.
For Bangladeshi families in Australia, that means the vaccine offers another option to discuss with their doctors before travelling home.
Mohammad Irfan Khan, a resident of Lakemba in Sydney, is planning to take his children to Bangladesh during an upcoming holiday.
He said reports about the dengue situation in Bangladesh, particularly infections and deaths among children, had been a source of anxiety.
With Qdenga now available, he plans to consult a doctor about whether his children should be vaccinated before the trip.
Another expatriate, Syed Ashraf Ahmed, said dengue was a growing concern among Bangladeshis living abroad as they frequently heard about relatives, friends and acquaintances becoming seriously ill back home.
The availability of vaccination before travelling to Bangladesh, he said, offered some reassurance to expatriate families.
Qdenga is a live-attenuated vaccine targeting all four dengue virus serotypes.
The vaccine is administered in two 0.5ml doses. Under Australian guidance, the doses are given three months apart, and completing the two-dose course is important for maximising protection.
There is currently insufficient evidence to support routine booster doses.
Dengue is transmitted primarily by infected Aedes mosquitoes.
Symptoms can include sudden fever, headache, muscle and joint pain, nausea, vomiting, fatigue and rash. While many infections are mild, severe dengue can become life-threatening.
Previous infection is particularly relevant because subsequent infection with another dengue serotype can, in some circumstances, carry a greater risk of severe disease.
Almost all dengue cases notified in Australia are acquired overseas, highlighting the risk faced by international travellers visiting countries where transmission is common.
Australia itself recorded 2,381 dengue notifications in 2024 and 1,863 in 2025, according to figures cited in the source material.
Health professionals stress, however, that vaccination does not replace protection against mosquito bites.
Travellers to Bangladesh and other dengue-affected destinations should continue using mosquito repellent, wearing protective clothing and taking other precautions to minimise exposure.
For Bangladeshi expatriates preparing to visit home, Qdenga therefore does not remove the dengue risk.
But it does provide something newly available in Australia: an additional preventive option that families can discuss with their doctors before travelling.

Policy dialogue calls for rights-based digital governance in Bangladesh
item.description:
A policy dialogue in Dhaka has called for stronger protection of privacy, freedom of expression and digital safety, along with greater institutional accountability, as Bangladesh’s use of technology continues to expand.
The “Policy Dialogue on Rights-Respecting Digital Governance in Bangladesh” brought together parliamentarians, policymakers, civil society representatives, journalists and young people to discuss building a safer, more inclusive and rights-based digital governance system.
The dialogue was organised by SERAC-Bangladesh, with support from DDI South Asia and Accountability Lab.
MP Anisur Rahaman of Madaripur-3, MP Salah Uddin of Gazipur-4 and reserved women’s seat MP Sherin Sultana attended the event, along with representatives from civil society, the media and youth groups.
The programme began with welcome remarks by Mizanur Rahman Akanda, project manager of SERAC-Bangladesh.
S M Shaikat, executive director of SERAC-Bangladesh, delivered the keynote presentation, focusing on protecting citizens, ensuring youth participation and strengthening institutional accountability to build a safe and rights-respecting digital Bangladesh.
The roundtable discussion was moderated by Md Salim Miah, director (programme) of SERAC-Bangladesh.
Freedom of expression was a key focus of the discussion.
Participants said the right to express opinions must be protected both online and offline, while stressing that exercising this right should not infringe on the rights, dignity, privacy or safety of others.
They called for a balanced approach to online expression, saying legitimate criticism and public debate should be protected, while threats, incitement to violence, fraud and other harmful activities should be addressed through clear, necessary and proportionate legal measures.
Participants also stressed the importance of accuracy and context in news and digital content, saying incomplete or one-sided reporting can mislead the public and distort perceptions of events.
Data privacy was another major concern at the dialogue.
Participants, including MPs, discussed the difficulties citizens face in correcting or updating their personal information.
They highlighted a contrast between the difficulties people often experience in correcting or updating their National Identity (NID) information and concerns that sensitive personal data may be obtained by unauthorised individuals for relatively small amounts of money.
The discussion referred to reported payments ranging from Tk30 to Tk250 for access to personal information.
Participants said institutions collecting and processing personal data should collect only information necessary for specific purposes and restrict access based on official responsibilities.
They also called for transparent and auditable records of who accesses and uses personal data, clear accountability for handling such information and effective remedies for unlawful access or misuse.
The dialogue also highlighted growing digital risks for children and young people.
Participants identified online harassment, identity misuse, manipulated and AI-generated content, and unauthorised use of personal information as major concerns.
They called for confidential and accessible complaint mechanisms, timely remedies and appropriate psychosocial support for young people facing online harm.
Participants also stressed that young people should not be treated merely as beneficiaries of digital policies. Instead, they should have a meaningful role in developing laws and policies affecting their digital lives, with their experiences and perspectives reflected in decision-making.
They further called for greater coordination among laws and policies on cybersecurity, personal data protection and national data management, as well as clear and accessible mechanisms for citizens to seek remedies when their rights are violated.
The dialogue also stressed the need to consult young people, civil society, technology experts, legal professionals, journalists and affected communities before introducing new digital laws and policies.
Participants identified several priorities for improving digital governance, including clear definitions of digital offences, proportionate enforcement of laws, stronger institutional accountability for personal data, safer digital participation for children, young people and women, meaningful public consultation and stronger parliamentary oversight.
They said Bangladesh’s digital transformation must be accompanied by stronger safeguards for fundamental rights, privacy, safety, dignity and freedom of expression.
They emphasised that digital governance should evolve alongside technological development while remaining accountable, transparent, inclusive and respectful of citizens’ rights.

item.title: German tourist loses bag after leaving it with railway official in Natore
item.description:
An 18-year-old German tourist lost his bag containing a laptop, camera and other valuables at Natore Railway Station on Wednesday after leaving it with a railway official before going to an ATM.
The tourist, identified as Kirill, arrived at the station by train from Bogra at around 4pm and left the bag in the waiting room before heading out to withdraw cash.
Kirill said he left his belongings with a railway official wearing a vest, who assured him that he would look after the items while he was away.
When he returned after withdrawing money, neither the official nor his bag and belongings could be found, he said.
Kirill said he searched in and around the station but could not locate his belongings.
According to Kirill, the iCloud location of his laptop showed that it was in the Naogaon area at around 6:40pm on Wednesday. The location data has raised hopes that the missing belongings may be recovered.
Kirill subsequently contacted railway authorities and was referred to Natore Sadar Police Station. He remained there for an extended period awaiting assistance and was seen breaking down in tears.
Natore Sadar Police Station Officer-in-Charge Monsur Rahman said the matter primarily falls under the jurisdiction of railway police.
“However, as the victim is a foreign national, we are treating the matter with the utmost importance,” he said.
The OC said police had already identified the location of the missing devices and sent a team there.
“We hope to recover Kirill’s laptop, camera and other missing belongings soon,” he added.

item.title: PM: Religion, identity must not stand in way of citizens’ rights
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Wednesday pledged to build a Bangladesh where religion, race or identity will not stand in the way of anyone’s rights and opportunities, with equal rights and dignity for every citizen.
“We want to build a Bangladesh where religion, race or identity will not stand in the way of people’s rights and opportunities. Our goal is to ensure equal rights and dignity for every citizen of the country,” he said.
The prime minister made the remarks at a view-exchange meeting with representatives of the Hindu and Buddhist communities at his office at the Secretariat, said his Deputy Press Secretary Shahadat Hossain Shadhin.
During the meeting, representatives of the Hindu community thanked the prime minister for extending the government holiday for Durga Puja, saying the decision has added to the festive joy of the Hindu community.
The representatives of the Hindu and Buddhist communities also raised various problems, needs and demands before the prime minister.
Tarique Rahman listened to their views and assured them that the government is sincerely working for the welfare of people from all communities.
“We will make our utmost efforts to do whatever is possible on behalf of the government. Your reasonable demands and problems will be considered with importance,” he said.
The Hindu community representatives invited the prime minister to visit different Durga Puja mandaps during five-day Durga Puja beginning on October 17.
Tarique Rahman extended greetings to members of the Hindu community on the occasion of Durga Puja and to members of the Buddhist community on the occasion of Kathin Chibar Dan.
He also wished peace, prosperity and welfare for all citizens of the country.
The representatives of the two communities, in turn, extended greetings to the prime minister on the occasion of their respective religious festivals.
Later, the prime minister handed over cheques – for Tk 5 crore to the Hindu Religious Welfare Trust for Durga Puja and Tk 3 crore to the Buddhist Religious Welfare Trust for the Buddhist religious festival.
The Hindu Religious Welfare Trust had sought Tk 4 crore for Durga Puja, while the prime minister approved Tk 5 crore as a special consideration.
Similarly, the Buddhist Religious Welfare Trust had sought Tk 2 crore for the Kathin Chibar Dan festival, but Tarique Rahman approved Tk 3 crore, also as a special consideration.
The government has also declared a three-day holiday from October 20 to 22 on the occasion of Durga Puja, allowing a five-day holiday as October 23 and 24 are weekend.
The allocated funds will be distributed among the beneficiaries through the Hindu Religious Welfare Trust and district administrations. The beneficiaries will be able to receive the money directly through their bank accounts.
Representatives of the Hindu and Buddhist communities thanked the prime minister for increasing the allocations and expressed their gratitude to the government.

item.title: ECNEC approves 13 projects involving Tk16,207.55cr
item.description:
The Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC) on Wednesday approved 13 projects involving a total cost of Tk16,207.55 crore, including a project to construct a 442-MW peak solar power plant at Rampal in Bagerhat.
Of the total project cost, Tk10,600.80 crore will come from government funds, Tk4,081.85 crore from project loans and Tk1,524.91 crore from concerned agencies’ own funds.
The approval came at the 5th meeting of the ECNEC held at Bangladesh Secretariat with prime minister and ECNEC Chairman Tarique Rahman in the chair.
Of the approved 13 projects, 10 are new, two are revised, and one involves extension of its implementation period.
State Minister for Planning Zonayed Abdur Rahim Saki briefed reporters after the meeting at the NEC Conference Room in the city’s Sher-e-Bangla Nagar area.
Under the Tk2,498.08-crore Rampal project, a 442-megawatt peak (MWp) solar power plant will be constructed at Rampal in Bagerhat, aimed at increasing renewable energy generation, diversifying the country’s primary fuel sources and reducing carbon emissions.
The Rampal 442 MWp Solar Power Plant Construction Project was proposed by the Power Division and will be implemented by the Bangladesh Power Development Board (BPDB). The project will be financed by BPDB from its own funds with Tk374.71 crore and from the Power Sector Development Fund Tk2,123.37 crore.
The Power Sector Development Fund loan would carry a 2% interest rate, with a one-year grace period and a 16-year repayment period.
The Planning Commission recommended that the project be implemented from September 2026 to March 2029.
In its assessment, the Planning Commission said the project would increase renewable-energy-based electricity generation and contribute to the government’s target of raising renewable energy’s share of the total energy mix to 20% by 2030.
Once the project is implemented, it would add 442MW of electricity to the national grid. Currently, the solar power generation in the country is 797MW out of the total on-grid power generation capacity of 28,827MW.
“The project will increase electricity generation based on renewable energy, which will help achieve the target of generating 20% of electricity from renewable sources by 2030,” said the Planning Commission official.
The Planning Commission said the project would strengthen energy security by diversifying primary fuel sources and reduce carbon emissions.
The proposed plant will be built on 918.50 acres of land in Block-B of Rampal that BPDB had already acquired. The Planning Commission said the use of BPDB-owned land would eliminate the need for fresh land acquisition and reduce project costs.
Electricity generated by the solar plant will be transmitted through the existing transmission infrastructure associated with the nearby Rampal coal-fired power plant. The project summary said this would allow the plant to be implemented relatively quickly and at lower cost.
BPDB acquired a total of 1,834 acres in Rampal in 2012 for development of a coal-fired power plant. The land was divided into Block-A, covering 915.50 acres, and Block-B covering 918.50 acres.
Bangladesh-India Friendship Power Company (Pvt) Ltd’s Maitree Super Thermal Power Plant was built in Block-A, while Block-B remains under BPDB.
Land development and boundary-wall construction have already been completed in Block-B, according to the project document.
The proposed solar plant will use solar photovoltaic modules with a minimum capacity of 640 watts peak. The project will also install grid-tied inverters with a cumulative capacity of 360MW, a pooling substation, a three-kilometre double-circuit 230-kV transmission line and three 230-kV bays, including one spare bay.
The largest component of the project cost, Tk1,238.61 crore, or around 50%, will go to solar photovoltaic modules and mounting structures.
Electrical equipment, including inverters, transformers and SCADA systems, will cost Tk732.25 crore.
The project summary said a feasibility study was conducted by the Infrastructure Investment Facilitation Company (IIFC) and found the project acceptable.
The project was included in the Annual Development Programme (ADP) for fiscal 2026-27 as an unapproved “green page” project.
The project is also aligned with the Five Year Strategic Framework for Reform and Development and the Sustainable Development Goal 7, which seeks to ensure access to affordable, reliable, sustainable and modern energy for all.
The day’s meeting also approved seven projects under the Ministry of Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives.
The projects are: improving road infrastructure and drainage in 18 wards under five newly incorporated regions of Dhaka South City Corporation; upgrading important infrastructure in Rangpur City Corporation; rehabilitating damaged roads in Rangpur City Corporation; and constructing roads, drains and footpaths in zones one to eight of Gazipur City Corporation.
The other projects under the ministry include a project for women’s skills development and entrepreneurship creation through cooperatives; rural infrastructure development in Sirajganj, Bogura and Naogaon districts; and the Important Urban Infrastructure Development Project (2nd phase), which was approved in its second revised form.
The ECNEC also approved the third revised project for procuring 35 commercial and eight auxiliary vessels for Bangladesh Inland Water Transport Corporation (BIWTC) and constructing two new slipways under the Ministry of Shipping.
Under the Ministry of Railways, the committee approved the Railway Capacity Expansion Project for procuring 30 metre-gauge diesel-electric locomotives for Bangladesh Railway.
It also approved a project under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to renovate and modernise the purchased chancery building in Paris, France, to make it suitable for use.
Two projects under the Ministry of Road Transport and Bridges also received approval. One involves constructing the Second Karatoya Bridge at the 15th kilometre of the Bhajanpur (Nijbari)-Atorkhari-Mainaguri-Amtali-Mirgachh-Panchagarh (Z-5060) road.
The other is the second revised Thanchi-Rimakri-Madak-Likri Road Construction Project.
Meanwhile, the ECNEC meeting was informed about a project costing less than Tk50 crore that had already received approval from the planning minister.
The project involves re-excavating the Nandahar and Harabati rivers and the Nunogola and Kharowa canals in Joypurhat district.
Ministers and state ministers concerned attended the meeting, while Planning Commission members and secretaries concerned were present.

item.title: Family planning campaign begins December 1 with ‘Two children’ slogan
item.description:
Health and Family Welfare Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Husain has announced a nationwide family planning campaign from December 1 to encourage people to limit family size.
Speaking to reporters at his office on Wednesday, the minister said the month-long awareness campaign would be conducted under the slogan, “No more than 2 children, one is better.”
The campaign will include rallies, fairs and various awareness programs across the country. Essential family planning supplies will also be delivered to households, he said.
“We will not just talk about it. We will also supply all the necessary materials. Tablets, contraceptives, pads—whatever is needed for family planning will be delivered to households,” the minister said.
He said the director general of the Directorate General of Family Planning and other officials concerned had been working over the past few days to prepare an implementation plan for the campaign.
Various programs will be organized at the district level to encourage people to adopt family planning practices, he added.
The minister said government spending must follow specific rules and procedures, which often takes time. As a result, many planned activities could not be implemented in the past.
“Work has now started afresh, and visible progress will be seen from the beginning of next year,” he said.
Describing family planning as one of the weaker areas of the country’s health sector, Sakhawat said the sector had failed to make the expected progress.
He also said there were several challenges to reducing the country’s birth rate.

item.title: 22-day ban on ilish catching begins at midnight
item.description:
The government has imposed a ban on ilish catching, selling, transporting and hoarding for the next 22 days, from Wednesday midnight to protect mother Hilsa and ensure safe breeding. The restriction will remain effective from Thursday to October 29. The decision was taken at a meeting of the National Taskforce Committee on Hilsa Resource Development held at the conference room of the Ministry of Fisheries and Livestock and the Ministry of Agriculture recently. According to the decision, transportation, storage, marketing, buying, selling and exchange of ilish will also remain prohibited across the country during the ban period. The government will provide Vulnerable Group Feeding (VGF) food assistance to fishermen who refrain from fishing during the period. Fishermen are starting to return from the deep sea to fish landing centres as the ban approaches. In Chandpur, a 22-day ban on fishing has begun in a 70-kilometre stretch of the Padma-Meghna rivers in Chandpur to ensure the safe breeding of ilish and protect the country's national fish resource. Ahead of the ban, many fishermen in Chandpur have already brought their boats and fishing nets ashore. While some are repairing their boats, others are busy mending damaged nets.
Meanwhile, district and upazila task forces have taken preparations to enforce the restriction. It was found that fishermen preparing for the 22-day fishing halt while visiting different fishing communities from Wednesday morning to noon.
The areas visited included Anandabazar in Tarpur Chandi Union of Sadar upazila, Tilabari on Jamuna Road, Ranagowal and Dokanghar areas of Puran Bazar, Ramdasdi and Baharia in Laxmipur Model Union, and the fishing village near Harina ferry terminal in Hanarchar Union. At Anandabazar, most fishermen were seen pulling their boats ashore, while some were repairing them. Similar scenes were observed at Baharia Bazar.
Fishermen in Ramdasdi were busy mending their nets while boat repair workers were seen working on several vessels near Harina ferry terminal.
Abul Kalam, 54, a fisherman from Anandabazar, said he had not caught much ilish in the river this season.
"I have already brought my boat ashore. I will put it back into the river after 22 days, depending on the availability of ilish," he said.
Khaleq Gazi, 52, a fisherman from Ramdasdi, said the government conducts the annual operation to protect mother ilish, but enforcement sometimes falls short because of inadequate planning.
"Patrolling should also be arranged in the canals connected to the Meghna so that unscrupulous fishermen cannot catch mother ilish," he said. Idris Ali, a fish trader from Baharia, said traders were ready to cooperate with the administration and police to ensure the safe spawning of ilish.
Veteran fish trader Sirajul Islam Sayed of Harina fish landing centre said the fishing ban should begin at the river's mouth near the sea before reaching the sanctuary areas, because many mother ilish are caught there and subsequently sent to markets. Chandpur Sadar Upazila Fisheries Officer Mirza Omar Faruk said several coordination meetings had already been held to ensure enforcement of the 22-day ban. "Awareness campaigns are being conducted in the Meghna coastal areas to warn fishermen against catching mother ilish," he said. Chandpur District Fisheries Officer Md Fakhrul Islam said district and upazila task forces would conduct regular drives in the sanctuary areas under Chandpur's river boundaries to protect ilish during the breeding season. "Anyone violating the law by entering the river for fishing will be brought under legal action," he added. He further said 41,000 registered fishermen who have been instructed to refrain from fishing during the ban have already received 25 kilograms of rice each as government assistance.

item.title: DU professor Jamal Uddin shown arrested in another anti-terrorism case after bail
item.description:
Professor AKM Jamal Uddin of Dhaka University’s Department of Sociology has been shown arrested in another anti-terrorism case after securing bail in a separate case.
Dhaka Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Jashita Islam passed the order on Wednesday following a petition by the investigating officer, said SI Rokonuzzaman of the prosecution department.
Police arrested Jamal Uddin on March 11 while he was taking part in a programme titled “Bangabandhu Peace March-2026” at Gulistan Zero Point in the capital.
He was later shown arrested in an anti-terrorism case filed with Paltan Model Police Station and sent to jail the same day. He recently secured bail from the High Court in that case.
On October 1, SI Md Nuruzzaman of Paltan Model Police Station sought an order to show Jamal Uddin arrested in another anti-terrorism case filed with the same police station.
The court fixed Wednesday for the hearing, and Jamal Uddin was brought before it from jail.
Public prosecutor Muhammad Shamsuddoha Sumon argued in favour of the police petition, while defence lawyer Md Khair Uddin Sikder opposed it.
After hearing both sides, the court reserved its order and later directed that Jamal Uddin be shown arrested in the case.
Advocate Md Khair Uddin Sikder said Jamal Uddin had secured bail from the High Court in an anti-terrorism case filed with Paltan Model Police Station. After the bail order was sent to the jail authorities, police sought to show him arrested in another case filed under the same law.
“He was shown arrested in the case today,” the lawyer said.
He also said Jamal Uddin is facing a case before the International Crimes Tribunal.
According to the case statement, members, financiers, advisers and instigators of the banned Bangladesh Chhatra League gathered in Gulistan, Baitul Mukarram and adjoining areas on May 18, 2025, allegedly to carry out acts of sabotage and destruction.
Police conducted a raid in front of Hotel Imperial, opposite the south gate of Baitul Mukarram, and detained several people. Around 140–150 unidentified people fled in different directions.
Police filed the anti-terrorism case with Paltan Model Police Station the same day.

Three arrested as adulterated, unapproved medicines made in Mohammadpur flat
item.description:
Adulterated and unapproved medicines, including children’s syrups, capsules and tablets, were being manufactured and stored for sale from a flat in Mohammadpur, Dhaka, where the Detective Branch (DB) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police seized medicines and manufacturing equipment worth around Tk1 crore and arrested three members of the gang during a raid.
The DB is also searching for doctors who prescribed the unapproved medicines to patients. DB chief and Additional Commissioner Md Shafiqul Islam said legal action would be taken against doctors found to be involved.
He shared the information in response to journalists’ questions at a press conference on Wednesday at the DMP Media Center.
Md Shafiqul Islam said the DB conducted the raid on Tuesday based on intelligence information at a third-floor flat in a building on Block-C of Dhaka Uddyan Road under Mohammadpur Police Station.
The arrested are Abdullah Al-Mamun, 42, Md Saju, 33, and Md Sajib, 26.
A large quantity of adulterated medicines was recovered, including syrups, capsules, shampoos, face washes, hygiene washes, soaps, powders and tablets.
The seized items include 192 bottles of KIDZ Omega Liquid 100ml syrup, 100 boxes of LACTOFLEX Capsules, 30 Facy GLOW Face Wash, 150 Detox Plus Shampoo, 70 Pedia Vox Kid Syrup, 300 strips of Osearc-CD capsules, 5kg of Oriva Hapes white powder, 50 BIOKET Active Shampoo, 800 KIDICARE Syrup Plus 100ml, 70 ZERO DAN Shampoo, 40 KETCOR-Z Shampoo and 10 Nutramide Syrup.
Also recovered were 150 empty packets of INTA CLEAN HYGIENE WASH, 80 unpackaged bottles of Hygiene Wash, 300 empty packets of PERMIMITE Soap, 80 Spiruva (Spirulina) leaflets, 100 polythene covers for face wash, 300 unlabelled syrup bottles, 400 white plastic containers, 100 unlabelled white tablets and 500 empty green capsule shells.
The DB also seized 3 cylinders used in making the medicines, a fuel-filling machine, 2 capsule-filling machines, 10kg of fuel in polythene, 6 capsule-filling machine parts and 2 label-attaching stamps.
The DB chief said several syrups and liquid products for children were among the recovered items. He said the adulterated and unapproved medicines could pose a serious risk to children’s lives and health.
A case was filed at Mohammadpur Police Station under the Special Powers Act against the 3 arrested, accusing them of keeping adulterated medicines in their possession for sale.
Asked how ordinary people can identify adulterated medicines, Md Shafiqul Islam said it is extremely difficult to recognize them. However, he said they can in many cases be identified by closely examining the medicine’s packaging and the relevant company’s packaging.
He said some of the medicines found in the raid are not in circulation in the country and, according to preliminary information, were imported from a neighboring country. He also said the medicines were being prescribed to patients through certain doctors.
Asked how much medicine the gang had already supplied to the market, given that medicines worth about Tk1 crore were seized, the DB chief said the matter was under investigation.
Documents found during the raid are being reviewed, he said, adding that everyone involved would be brought under the law after the investigation.
Md Shafiqul Islam said the seized medicines included foreign products, and whether they were legally imported into the country was also being investigated.
The DB chief said some medicines for children were also found during the raid. Among them, he identified a syrup named Kidocare as counterfeit. Some medicines for children related to Kid Omega and Vitamin D3 were also seized.

Shama Obaed: Cox’s Bazar insecurity ‘cannot become the new normal’
item.description:
Seeking a genuine solution to the Rohingya crisis, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam on Wednesday warned that rising crime and insecurity affecting Cox’s Bazar host communities “cannot be allowed to become the new normal.”
She said the solution lies in Myanmar and that Bangladesh cannot sustain the crisis indefinitely.
The state minister urged the international community to move from statements of support to actionable and predictable assistance.
She addressed the National Policy Dissemination Program on “Uncertain Return: Rohingya Voices on Repatriation Barriers,” organized by the Department of Criminology and the Criminology Research Forum of the University of Dhaka, as chief guest at the Senate Bhaban, University of Dhaka.
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam addresses the National Policy Dissemination Programme on ’Uncertain Return: Rohingya Voices on Repatriation Barriers’ at the Senate Bhaban, University of Dhaka, on Wednesday, October 7, 2026. Photo: UNB
In her speech as the chief guest, the state minister recalled the address of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman at the 81st UNGA and highlighted the five urgent priorities he set before the international community: from a credible roadmap for sustainable repatriation to an end to violence, justice, accountability and stronger action against transnational crimes.
She noted the formation of a National Strategy Formulation Committee to guide the Rohingyas’ safe and dignified return.
Referring to the study conducted by the Department of Criminology on the envisaged return of the forcibly displaced Myanmar nationals (FDMNs), she mentioned that the Rohingyas are not rejecting Myanmar as their home.
They are rejecting a return to the conditions that forced them to flee.
She identified recognition and identity, land and property, security, and trust with credible guarantees as the pillars of a credible roadmap, adding that “repatriation is an act of trust” and that the Rohingyas are “asking for rights, not charity.”
Earlier, the research team introduced the research, which had surveyed 816 Rohingya respondents across 17 camp sites in Ukhiya, Cox’s Bazar.
They had also conducted 72 in-depth interviews with stakeholders involved in the repatriation process.
The state minister also distributed prizes among winners of an "Essay Competition" organized by the Department of Criminology.

item.title: Mahdi Amin: Govt committed to workers’ rights, better working conditions
item.description:
Prime Minister’s Adviser on Labour and Employment Mahdi Amin has said the government is committed to protecting workers’ rights, creating jobs and ensuring better working conditions.
“Protecting workers’ rights and creating widespread employment opportunities are the government’s priorities,” he said.
He made the remarks during a courtesy meeting with a high-level delegation from the International Trade Union Confederation (ITUC) and the International Organisation of Employers (IOE) at the Ministry of Labour and Employment at the Secretariat on Wednesday.
The meeting discussed the economic role of export processing zones (EPZs) and the implementation of laws and policies to preserve their distinct status while sustaining employment, Mahdi Amin said.
He said the government has been working to strengthen workers’ rights and would consider recommendations from international organisations such as the ITUC and IOE.
“Ensuring fair and safe workplaces, improving employer-worker relations and establishing effective social dialogue are among the government’s key priorities,” he said.
The government is also working to expand decent employment opportunities and develop the skills of the workforce, he added.
Labour and Employment Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury was present at the meeting.
The visiting delegation included ITUC General Secretary Luc Triangle, IOE Vice-Chair Kaiser Moyane, ILO Governing Body member Jess Vogt and ILO Country Director Max Tunon, among others.
Welcoming the delegation, Mahdi Amin said the visit and tripartite discussions among the government, workers and employers would help assess progress and chart the way forward in implementing the ILO roadmap.
“Under the strong leadership of Tarique Rahman, the government is committed to workers’ welfare, decent work and productive employment,” he said.
Mahdi Amin said the newly elected government amended the Bangladesh Labour Act during the first session of parliament to bring it in line with current needs.
He said Bangladesh had recently ratified ILO Conventions 155, 187 and 189 to uphold international standards on workers’ rights and protection.
The government has also taken steps to strengthen labour administration, expedite dispute resolution and establish effective social dialogue among stakeholders, he added.
“Our main goal now is to quickly formulate the Bangladesh Labour Rules and ensure effective implementation of the amended Labour Act,” Mahdi Amin said.
He said the government was committed to turning its pledges into tangible improvements in the lives of workers.
The ITUC and IOE delegations praised recent labour-sector reforms, particularly amendments to the Labour Act, the streamlined trade union registration process, measures to improve occupational health and safety, and initiatives to ensure fair wages.

item.title: Benin full of pride at role in Messi's last dance
item.description:
Football fans in Benin declared that it was "an honour" that the west African nation provided the opposition for Lionel Messi's final international appearance -- and most only had eyes for the Argentinian superstar.
Benin lost 3-0 in Buenos Aires in front of more than 80,000 spectators on Tuesday -- but the result was almost meaningless on a night on which one of the world's greatest ever players made his international farewell.
From neighbourhood to neighbourhood, screens had sprung up in restaurants and bars in the Beninese capital Cotonou so as not to miss a moment of the historic occasion.
"We're looking for a screen, even if we have to stand," said one young worker, hurrying like many others to find a spot in time to watch the action from Argentina that kicked off at midnight local time in Benin.
Although a few "Go Benin" chants rang out during the national anthems, those watching in Benin really only had eyes for 39-year-old Messi, aware that they were witnessing a historic moment in world football.
"It's an honour that Benin is the last team Messi faces," said Sylvestre Dagbedji, 34, a security guard and self-declared Messi fan.
"We'll always remember that it was against Benin that he retired from international football," he added.
Sitting nearby, Armand Folly, 27, a motorcycle taxi driver, said: "It's going to be tough for us Beninese. Messi is a great player. I'm so proud of him for his career."
During the match, supporters cheered the Cheetahs' efforts to break through the Argentinian rearguard, but applauded the eight-time Ballon d'Or winner and former Barcelona forward every time he received the ball.
"I'm sad because Messi won't play anymore. He was excellent at Barca, I don't know who will be able to play like him again," said Toussain Kpadonou, a craftsman, who was gathered with around a hundred people in front of a giant screen.
The younger fans were also delighted to see the TV coverage of the final international appearance of a player who has lit up the football world for two decades.
"Messi is a god of football, the best player in the world. He performed so well throughout his entire career, from Barca to Inter Miami," said Destin Avere, 17.
In the 71st minute of the game, having already provided two assists, Messi stepped up to take the penalty to round out the score -- and the crowd in Benin erupted when the ball hit the back of the net.
Benin's defeat was already forgotten -- the crowd's only thought was for Messi. "We're going to miss him," said Armand Folly.
