Dhaka Tribune journalist Shahrukh selected for COP31 fellowship
item.description:
Dhaka Tribune journalist Shaikh Shahrukh Farhan has been selected for the 2026 Climate Change Media Partnership (CCMP) Reporting Fellowship to cover the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, from November 9 to 20.
Shahrukh is among 14 journalists and two independent creator-journalists selected from Asia, Africa, Europe, Latin America and the Pacific through an international selection process.
The fellowship is jointly organized by the Earth Journalism Network (EJN), Informed Earth and the Stanley Center for Peace and Security.
Under the program, the selected journalists will report directly from the UN climate negotiations, covering international climate policy and its implications for audiences in their respective countries.
For Bangladesh, Shahrukh’s reporting is expected to focus on the implications of COP31 negotiations for a country facing climate-related challenges, including rising temperatures, extreme weather, sea-level rise and coastal erosion.
The fellowship will enable participants to cover negotiations and developments involving climate finance, infrastructure, greenhouse gas emissions reduction, mitigation and adaptation.
Participants will also receive professional guidance from journalists and media trainers Joydeep Gupta, Fermín Koop and Imelda Abaño.
The program brings together journalists from 15 countries, providing opportunities to exchange reporting experiences and strengthen their understanding of international climate negotiations.
Other selected fellows include Anandabhuwana from Indonesia, Angelica Maria Daza Romero from Colombia, Aparna Bose from India, Aria Deemie from Liberia, Hammad S from Pakistan, Lerato Mutsila from South Africa, María de los Ángeles Graterol Camacho from Venezuela, Maria Vasileva Petrova-Galabova from Bulgaria, Nadia Luna from Argentina, Nathalie Iriarte Villavicencio from Bolivia, Nkoli Omhoudu from Nigeria, Noel Charles Piringi from Solomon Islands, Francis Ontomwa from Kenya and Zenebe Hailu Gemechu from Ethiopia.
Shahrukh has more than 12 years of experience in journalism, covering public policy, governance, climate change, environmental protection, energy, ICT and telecommunications, elections, migration, women and children, and sustainable development.
His reporting interests include climate adaptation, renewable energy, energy security, environmental pollution, biodiversity conservation, climate finance and issues affecting climate-vulnerable communities.
COP31, the 31st Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, is scheduled to take place in Antalya from November 9 to 20.
The conference will bring together government representatives, international organizations, researchers, civil society groups and other stakeholders for negotiations on global climate action.
Key issues expected to feature in reporting from the conference include countries’ climate commitments, progress on previous agreements, climate finance, mitigation and adaptation.

item.title: Dinajpur entrepreneur cultivates black rice for first time in Bochaganj
item.description:
A young entrepreneur has experimentally cultivated Vietnamese black rice for the first time in Bochaganj upazila of Dinajpur, drawing interest from local farmers over its potential profitability.
Rakibul Haque, a resident of Dighori village in Nafanagar Union who cultivated the crop on 33 decimals of leased land, said he became interested in black rice after learning about it online. He first bought 1kg of rice for Tk550 to taste it before deciding to cultivate the crop. He later purchased 2kg of seeds online for Tk1,150 and raised seedlings.
Unable to secure permission to use his family’s ancestral land, he leased 33 decimals for Tk24,000 and transplanted the seedlings on July 9. The crop is expected to be harvested between October 10 and 12. “Black rice does not require additional fertiliser, irrigation or special care compared with conventional rice,” Rakibul said.
He expects to harvest 18-20 maunds of rice from the plot. With black rice currently selling for around Tk400 per kg, he expects potential sales of about Tk320,000 if the projected yield and market price are achieved.
According to the agriculture department, black rice is rich in antioxidants, anthocyanin, fibre and iron. Its nutritional value has made it popular among health-conscious consumers, while it is also sought after by Chinese restaurants.
Local residents have been visiting the field ahead of the harvest, and some have contacted Rakibul to collect seeds for future cultivation. Local farmers Shambhu Roy and Jewel said they were interested in growing black rice after seeing the crop’s growth and condition.
Rakibul’s father, Aminul Haque, initially opposed the project, calling his son’s internet-inspired venture “madness” and refusing to provide ancestral land. He has since changed his mind after seeing the crop’s progress. “I am ready to support my son in any way I can after seeing the success of his initiative,” he said.
Bochaganj Upazila Agriculture Officer Nayan Kumar Saha said wider cultivation of the nutrient-rich rice could contribute to the country’s agricultural economy.
Upazila Nirbahi Officer Md Maruf Hasan said this was the first black rice cultivation in Bochaganj. “If production and marketing can be properly ensured, it could be a profitable crop for farmers,” he said.

item.title: Fruit prices soar in Bandarban
item.description:
Prices of various fruits have surged in Bandarban, with traders attributing the rise in prices of oranges, maltas and pomegranates to increased demand amid a dengue outbreak.
Prices of oranges and maltas have increased by up to Tk200 per kilogram in the past two weeks, putting fruits beyond the reach of many patients and middle-income families.
A visit to Bandarban’s fruit market on Friday found that the price of malta had risen from Tk270 to Tk450 per kg, while Chinese oranges increased from Tk280 to Tk500. Pomegranates rose from Tk380 to Tk460 per kg.
Gala apples increased from Tk340 to Tk360, Fuji Gala apples from Tk320 to Tk330, pears from Tk300 to Tk310 and red grapes from Tk400 to Tk440 per kg.
White grapes, which were previously unavailable in the market, are now selling for Tk500 per kg. Watermelon prices have also risen from Tk80 to Tk90 per kg.
Mohammad Abdul Alim of Siddiq Store, a fruit trader at Bandarban market, said demand had not increased significantly. “Fruit prices are high because our purchase costs have increased. So, we have to sell them at higher prices,” he said.
Papayas, commonly included in the diets of dengue patients, are also in short supply. Meanwhile, large coconuts have risen from Tk120 to Tk160 each, while small ones now sell for Tk120, up from Tk110.
Champak Das, a coconut trader, said demand for coconuts had increased amid the dengue outbreak while supplies had fallen. “When supply falls against higher demand, prices go up. We have little scope to sell them at lower prices,” he said.
According to the Bandarban civil surgeon’s office, 1,095 people have contracted dengue in the district between January 1 and October 2. Two people have died, both from Rowangchhari upazila.
Akim Bom, who was buying fruit for a patient, said the price hikes were making it increasingly difficult for families to afford fruit. “If prices keep rising like this, we may not be able to continue buying fruit,” he said.
Traders expect prices of imported fruits to ease somewhat toward the end of October as the winter season begins and supplies increase.

item.title: ‘Shanti Nibas’ remains closed for three years in Rajshahi, Khulna
item.description:
A ‘Shanti Nibas’ (old home), built by the government for abandoned and destitute elderly people in Rajshahi at a cost of nearly Tk 9 crore, has remained closed for three years. The Shanti Nibas in Baya area of Paba upazila was inaugurated three years ago with facilities to accommodate 25 elderly people, including healthcare, lift, recreation, exercise, prayer, and training facilities.
But not a single elderly person has been admitted to the facility due to a lack of manpower recruitment. Besides, an organogram for its operation has yet to be prepared.
The facility was built under a government program to provide safe accommodation and care for people aged over 60 who are abandoned, destitute, or have no one to look after them. In 2020, Department of Social Services took up a project to build 25-bed Shanti Nibas facilities on the premises of government children’s homes in eight divisions.
In Rajshahi, a three-storey building with a five-storey foundation was constructed on 1,621 square metres of land on the western side of Paba Government Children’s Home (Boys). It has 25 beds, a lift, reception and visitors’ rooms, a healthcare corner, recreation and exercise equipment, a prayer room, a training corner, a production unit, and a coffee corner.
Despite the infrastructure being ready, the facility has remained closed to its intended beneficiaries. Long periods of disuse have left dust on furniture and equipment, while moss has formed on parts of the walls. Some equipment is also at risk of deterioration.
Rajshahi Social Services Department Deputy Director Monira Khatun said the facility could not be opened because the necessary manpower had not been appointed. “An organogram for recruiting the required manpower has not even been prepared. So far, we have not been able to admit any elderly person,” she said.
Besides, a Shanti Nibas built in Khulna to provide shelter for abandoned and destitute elderly people has remained closed for nearly three years due to a lack of staff appointments and an official office code.
The facility, built inside the government children’s family premises in Maheshwarpasha, was formally inaugurated on November 14, 2023. However, it has yet to accommodate a single resident. The three-storey building, constructed on a five-storey foundation, can house 25 elderly people.
A recent visit found moss on the stairs, balconies and walls, while railings have started rusting. Furniture and equipment have also been gathering dust. Some fire extinguishers at the facility have expired.
The ground floor has a doctors’ room equipped with a bed, wheelchairs and a therapy bed, while exercise equipment remains unused in the gym. The dining room has two large tables.
“The furniture and other equipment are deteriorating to some extent as the facility has remained unused for so long,” said Khan Motahar Hossain, deputy director of the divisional social services office. “It could not be opened due to the absence of staff appointments and an office code,” he added.

item.title: WHO: Heart disease remains world’s biggest killer
item.description:
Ischaemic heart disease is still the world's deadliest condition; meanwhile, Covid-19 has been among the global top 10 causes of death for the first time since the pandemic began, according to the latest World Health Organization (WHO) data released on Friday.
In 2023, the top 10 causes of death made up 33 million out of 61 million deaths worldwide, which is 54% of the total.
Eight of these ten were noncommunicable diseases (NCDs), and they alone caused 47% of all deaths.
Ischaemic heart disease led to 9.5 million deaths in 2023, which is about 16% of deaths worldwide.
Since 2000, deaths from this disease have increased by 3 million, the biggest rise among all causes.
Stroke was the second leading cause, with about 6.8 million deaths (11%), followed by chronic obstructive pulmonary disease at 3.6 million (6%).
Lower respiratory infections were fourth and became the world's deadliest communicable disease again, killing 2.7 million people, which is back to pre-pandemic 2019 levels.
Alzheimer's disease and other dementias were the fifth leading cause, with 2.1 million deaths. Two-thirds of those who died were women.
Diabetes was sixth, causing 2 million deaths, which is more than twice the number in 2000.
Lung cancers were seventh, with deaths rising from 1.1 million in 2000 to 1.8 million.
Kidney diseases moved from seventeenth to ninth place, with deaths increasing by 86% since 2000.
Covid-19 was the top cause of death worldwide in 2021, with about 9.4 million deaths. By 2023, direct deaths dropped to 0.9 million, making it the fourteenth leading cause.
HIV/AIDS deaths have dropped by 62% since 2000, moving from seventh to twenty-second place.
Bangladesh is in the World Bank's lower-middle-income group, where the WHO reports a mixed disease burden.
In this group, five of the top ten causes of death were NCDs, four were communicable, maternal, neonatal, or nutritional conditions, and one was road injury.
Between 2000 and 2023, deaths from ischaemic heart disease, stroke, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease roughly doubled. These now rank in the top three.
Diabetes moved from fifteenth to fifth place, with deaths more than tripling.
Tuberculosis and diarrhoeal diseases are still in the top 10 for this group, but deaths from both have dropped by more than half over the period.
However, the WHO report does not provide country-level figures for Bangladesh.
The report shows big differences by income level.
In low-income countries, seven of the top ten causes of death were communicable diseases, with lower respiratory infections leading for most years since about 2010.
Annual deaths from the disease have exceeded 350,000 throughout 2000-2023, with no notable downward trend.
In upper-middle-income countries, lung cancer deaths more than doubled, with 520,000 more deaths.
Covid-19 is still in the top 10 only in this group.
In high-income countries, NCDs made up nine of the ten leading causes of death.
Deaths from heart disease and stroke fell by 18% and 26%, respectively, since 2000, though dementia deaths nearly quadrupled and it became the third leading cause of death.
The WHO emphasized that reliable mortality data is crucial for setting health priorities, allocating resources, and making policies in areas like transport, food, agriculture, and environmental protection.
However, it noted that data collection remains a major challenge, especially in many low-income countries where systems are often fragmented, incomplete, or inconsistent.

item.title: UK maritime agency: Oil tankers attacked in Hormuz strait
item.description:
Two oil tankers have been struck by "unidentified projectiles" in the Strait of Hormuz region, a British maritime agency said Friday, in the latest threat to shipping in the waterway.
The Hormuz passage, through which a fifth of the world's oil and LNG passed before the US and Israel launched strikes against Iran in late February and sparked the Middle East war, remains at the heart of the conflict.
Tehran has been blocking the passage of commercial ships, firing on vessels it accuses of unauthorised crossings.
Washington responded with a counterblockade of Iranian ports in an effort to prevent Tehran from exporting its oil.
The first attack caused "a small fire and blackout onboard", the UK Maritime Trade Operations agency said Friday, adding that the fire was later extinguished.
There were no reported casualties or environmental impact, it added.
The vessel, which was exiting the strait, was able to resume its journey, UKMTO said, without specifying the ship's ports of origin and destination.
Hours later, another crude oil tanker reported being struck by an "unknown projectile" east of Oman, with all crew safe and no environmental damage reported, according to the UKMTO.
The agency said authorities were investigating the incidents.

Uranium consignment reaches Rooppur nuclear power plant amid tight security
item.description:
A uranium consignment for the second unit of Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant reached the project site in Pabna on Saturday afternoon amid tight security.
Three uranium-laden lorries arrived at the nuclear power plant site around 12:25pm after leaving Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka at around 7:15am under the security escort of the Bangladesh Army, said Pabna Deputy Commissioner Aminul Islam.
The consignment is the first shipment of uranium for the second unit of the Rooppur plant.
A special cargo aircraft carrying the uranium landed at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport at around 11:44pm on Friday.
After completing the necessary formalities, the uranium was transported to Rooppur in three lorries while another vehicle carried other equipment.
A team of specialists who had arrived from Russia also accompanied the consignment.
Members of the Bangladesh Army, police and various intelligence agencies were deployed to ensure security during the transportation.
The flight carrying uranium for Rooppur plant was scheduled to arrive on September 24 but was not given permission to use Pakistani airspace.
According to project officials, a total of nine uranium consignments are scheduled to be brought to Bangladesh — seven for the second unit and two for the refuelling of the first unit.
All the consignments are scheduled to be delivered by December.
Fuel for the first unit of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant was brought to Bangladesh in 2023.
The Rooppur plant, comprising two 1,200-megawatt units, has a total generation capacity of 2,400MW.
Construction of the plant began in 2013 with Russian assistance at an estimated cost of more than Tk1.13 lakh crore.
Nuclear Power Plant Company Bangladesh Ltd (NPCBL) Managing Director Dr Zahidul Hasan said testing of the 16-megawatt high-pressure system under the reactor protection and safety-related system was successfully completed on Wednesday following the replacement of a defective valve.

North Korea fires ballistic missile after Seoul’s apology demand
item.description:
North Korea fired a ballistic missile, Seoul’s military said Saturday, days after demanding an apology for a blast that wounded three South Korean soldiers in the DMZ that it blames on the North.
Pyongyang has denied responsibility for last month’s explosion inside the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) and called South Korea “despicable” on Friday, undercutting overtures by Seoul’s civilian leadership seeking a return to dialogue.
Early Saturday, “our military detected a ballistic missile launched from the Wonsan area of North Korea toward the East Sea,” Seoul’s Joint Chiefs of Staff said, referring to the body of water also known as the Sea of Japan.
“South Korea, the US, and Japan are maintaining a robust defense posture through close information sharing regarding North Korean ballistic missiles,” it said, adding the missile flew more than 700 kilometers (435 miles).
Seoul and the US-led United Nations Command found that last month’s explosion inside the DMZ, the heavily mined buffer dividing the two Koreas since their 1953 armistice, was caused by North Korean mines laid on the South side of the border.
North Korea’s military has laid mines and built anti-tank barriers along the frontier as part of efforts to permanently seal it off following leader Kim Jong Un’s designation of South Korea as his country’s “principal enemy” in 2024.
The mines responsible for the blast, which left three soldiers wounded, were believed to have been laid as part of Pyongyang’s border fortification work, according to South Korea’s defense minister Kang Shin-chul.
South Korea’s dovish President Lee Jae Myung had urged Pyongyang on Thursday to return to dialogue, despite his military demanding an apology a day earlier.
Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of North Korea’s leader, responded by calling Seoul “really despicable” on Friday and once again denied Pyongyang was behind the blasts.
She ridiculed Lee’s latest overture, calling it “the climax of the farce that everyone should watch” and said the military’s demand her country apologize was “quite ridiculous.”
Kim also warned Pyongyang was “ready for anything” Seoul might do over the mine blast -- remarks followed the next morning by North Korea’s ballistic missile launch.
Analysts said the launch would be viewed as a show of force in response to the South Korean government’s diplomatic efforts, effectively rejecting engagement.
“Seoul called for easing tensions, but Pyongyang answered by escalating them,” Yang Moo-jin, former president of the University of North Korean Studies in Seoul, told AFP.
“The message is that the North is pursuing... confrontation in response to goodwill,” he added.
South Korea’s defense minister said on Tuesday the military had “a range of necessary measures at our disposal, and we will implement them in stages” to respond to the DMZ incident, without providing further detail.
The South’s Unification Minister, Chung Dong-young, also proposed talks to address issues along the border to Pyongyang on Friday.
Kim Yo Jong, however, dismissed Chung’s suggestion of talks as a “wild dream and unilateral jargon.”
The flare-up comes at a sensitive time when US President Donald Trump’s recent overtures to Pyongyang have raised concerns that Seoul -- an ally of Washington -- could be sidelined in potential nuclear talks involving the North.
South Korea’s opposition People Power Party on Friday accused Lee of failing to criticize Pyongyang when warranted even as he takes a hard line on Ukraine for publicly disclosing the transfer of North Korean prisoners of war, an arrangement Seoul believed should be confidential.
“South Korean soldiers have been injured, and far from receiving an apology, we have been mocked by North Korea,” the opposition party said in a statement.
“We fail to see how selectively turning a blind eye to North Korea serves South Korea’s dignity or the safety of its people.”

item.description:
Dhaka, the densely populated capital of Bangladesh, ranked third among the world’s most polluted cities on Saturday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) of 170 at 9:14am.
The city’s air was classified as "unhealthy", indicating a health threat, according to the AQI report.
Pakistan’s Lahore, India’s Kolkata and Delhi occupied the first, second, and fourth spots on the list, with AQI scores of 214, 190, and 168 respectively.
According to the AQI scale, a reading between 50 and 100 is considered "moderate", with generally acceptable air quality, though sensitive individuals should limit prolonged outdoor exertion. AQI levels of 101–150 are "unhealthy for sensitive groups", 151–200 are " unhealthy", 201–300 are "very unhealthy", and readings above 301 are considered "hazardous", posing severe health risks.
The AQI, which reports daily air quality, informs residents how clean or polluted the air is and highlights potential health effects. In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five key pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2), and ozone.
Dhaka has long struggled with air pollution. Air quality usually deteriorates in winter and improves during the monsoon season.
The World Health Organization (WHO) estimates that air pollution causes about seven million deaths worldwide each year, primarily from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer, and acute respiratory infections.

item.title: CUET students continue protest, rally on holiday
item.description:
The movement by teachers, officers, employees and students of Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology (CUET) demanding the reinstatement of Professor Abu Sadat Mohammad Sayem as vice-chancellor continued on Friday, with students staging a protest rally on campus.
The rally began around 2:30pm from in front of the university’s Teachers-Students Centre, passed through several campus roads and ended at the main gate. Students chanted slogans demanding Professor Sayem’s reinstatement.
Since the movement began, students have held various protest programmes, including torch processions, red-card demonstrations, “Why 56?”, “Testimony in White Sarees,” a procession wearing masks depicting the former vice-chancellor, protests with black cloth over their eyes, and a “Protest Concert.”
Zulkarnaine Mihad, a fourth-year student of the Department of Mechanical Engineering who joined the rally, said, “Today marks the 11th day of our movement. No action has yet been taken in response to our demand. Classes and examinations remain suspended. Our movement will continue until our demand is met.”
Students launched the movement the same day, protesting the change just 56 days after Professor Sayem assumed office. They began a “complete shutdown” the following day, September 22.
After 11 days of protests, no resolution has yet been reached over their demand to reinstate Professor Sayem.

item.title: Ex-lawmaker Akhtaruzzaman sued over alleged airport assault, disorder
item.description:
A case has been filed against Major (retd) Akhtaruzzaman, a former lawmaker, on charges of obstructing government duties, creating disorder at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport and assaulting a security official.
Airport security officer Md Shahriar Alam Sajib filed the case with Airport Police Station on Friday under several sections of the Code of Criminal Procedure, an official said.
According to the First Information Report (FIR), the incident took place around 10:40am on Thursday after passengers of a Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight (BG-338) arriving from Madina faced a shortage of trolleys and delays in collecting their baggage at No 8 baggage belt amid heavy passenger pressure.
As frustration and tension among the passengers escalated, Airport Executive Director Group Captain SM Ragib Samad went to the spot to bring the situation under control following a request from Dhaka-5 MP Mohammad Kamal Hossain.
The FIR said that while Ragib Samad was trying to calm the situation, Akhtaruzzaman, who was expelled from BNP several times and joined Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami in December 2025, allegedly moved towards him aggressively, abused him and threatened to beat him and throw him out of the airport by the neck.
He also allegedly made offensive remarks about the civil aviation and tourism minister.
The situation worsened when protocol assistants accompanying Akhtaruzzaman started recording videos on mobile phones in the airport's restricted Key Point Installation (KPI) area.
When security supervisor Warrant Officer Mohammad Kamal Uddin asked them to stop recording, Akhtaruzzaman allegedly abused him and physically assaulted him.
The FIR further alleged that Akhtaruzzaman threw bottles of holy Zamzam water collected by other passengers from their trolleys, allegedly causing damage, and behaved aggressively towards a representative of Biman Bangladesh Airlines.
Police said they will collect CCTV footage, statements from eyewitnesses and other evidence as part of the investigation and take legal action based on the findings.

item.title: Pharmacist injured in attack by expelled Jubo Dal leader in Banglamotor
item.description:
A pharmacist was injured after an expelled Jubo Dal leader allegedly attacked him with a pistol in Banglamotor, Dhaka, on Thursday night.
The injured man, Md Sohan, 35, received treatment at Dhaka Medical College Hospital.
Police detained four people in connection with the incident, including expelled Jubo Dal leader Ferdous Ahmed Saimon.
Sohan said Ferdous and several associates blocked his way in an alley north of Rupayan Tower in Banglamotor around Thursday night.
During an argument, Ferdous allegedly hit Sohan on the head with the butt of a pistol, leaving him bleeding.
Ferdous then allegedly fired two blank shots to create panic, Sohan said.
Hearing the gunshots, local residents came forward, prompting Ferdous and his associates to enter a nearby building. Residents gathered outside the building and protested the incident.
A video of the protest has circulated on social media. In the video, locals allege that Ferdous has long been extorting money in the area and attacking people who refuse to pay.
Tejgaon Division Deputy Commissioner Md Ibne Mizan said Ferdous Ahmed and two of his associates were detained and taken to Tejgaon Industrial Area police station around midnight.
Police said Sohan was beaten and struck on the head during an argument. Locals then surrounded Saimon and his associates.
Police went to the scene after being informed and brought the situation under control. Additional police were later deployed, and the situation returned to normal during the night.

item.title: Klopp earns first Germany win as Portugal progresses without Ronaldo
item.description:
Jürgen Klopp secured his first victory as Germany coach, while Portugal advanced with a convincing win over Denmark without veteran forward Cristiano Ronaldo in the Nations League on Thursday.
Florian Wirtz scored as Germany beat Serbia 2-0 in Munich, giving Klopp his first victory in his third match in charge and avoiding an unwanted record.
The 59-year-old had opened his tenure with a 1-1 draw against the Netherlands before Germany suffered a surprise 1-0 loss to Greece on Sunday.
Germany produced a disciplined and energetic performance against Serbia, reflecting the high-intensity style Klopp wants to establish.
“That's going in my archive. We'll make a video out of it now,” Klopp said. “That's how we want to play.”
Germany created several chances before Tom Bischof opened the scoring in the 39th minute, finishing the rebound after Wirtz's effort struck the post.
Klopp introduced Said El Mala after halftime for his Germany debut. Goalkeeper Jonas Urbig and Freiburg forward Derry Scherhant also made their international debuts.
Wirtz doubled Germany's lead after receiving Maximilian Mittelstädt's cross. He controlled the ball past a defender with his first touch before finding the inside of the right post with his second.
“It was important to win again, just for the spirit in the team, and to send a signal out that we're good football players and also a good football nation,” Wirtz said.
Netherlands held by Greece
Tijjani Reijnders scored in the 89th minute as the Netherlands came from behind to draw 2-2 with Greece in Thessaloniki in the other Group A2 match.
Fotis Ioannidis scored one goal and assisted on the other for Greece, while Virgil van Dijk scored before Reijnders rescued a point for the Netherlands.
The Dutch side had also needed a late equalizer in its previous match against Germany.
Greece remained top of Group A2 after recording away wins over Serbia and Germany.
Portugal wins without Ronaldo
Portugal defeated Denmark 4-2 in Copenhagen as João Félix sealed the victory late, with Ronaldo absent from the squad.
Ronaldo left the team a day earlier following an apparent dispute with coach Jorge Jesus, raising questions over his future with the national side.
Gonçalo Ramos, who replaced the 41-year-old forward, assisted João Cancelo for Portugal's opening goal before scoring the team's second two minutes after Mikkel Damsgaard equalized in the 23rd minute.

item.title: Misty’s parliamentary seat declared vacant
item.description:
BNP reserved-seat MP Ferdousi Ahmed Misty has resigned, leaving her parliamentary seat vacant, according to a notification issued by the Parliament Secretariat on Thursday.
The notification, issued by the Law Drafting Branch-2 of the Legislative Support Wing, said Misty’s resignation took effect on Thursday, leaving parliamentary seat No 323 vacant under Article 67(2) of the Constitution.
Parliament Secretariat Secretary Barrister Md Golam Sarwar Bhuiyan signed the notification.
Copies were sent to the Cabinet Division, Election Commission Secretariat and other relevant offices for necessary action.
Under Rule 177 of the Rules of Procedure of Parliament, a lawmaker wishing to resign must submit a written resignation addressed to the Speaker and signed by the member. The resignation takes effect and the seat becomes vacant once the letter reaches the Speaker, in accordance with Article 67(2) of the Constitution.
Earlier on Thursday afternoon, Misty submitted her resignation letter to the Speaker.
The resignation came after Prime Minister Tarique Rahman directed her to step down following allegations of her involvement in an attack and vandalism at the Radda MCH-FP Centre in Mirpur, Dhaka.
She subsequently went to Parliament and submitted her resignation letter.

item.title: President seeks more Australian support to energy security
item.description:
President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on Thursday sought more support from Australia in the areas of energy security, skilled workforce migration, technical education, investment and economic partnership.
The president made the call when Australian High Commissioner Susan Ryle paid a courtesy call on him at Bangabhaban here today, President's Press Secretary Md Sarwar Alam said.
During the meeting, the Australian High Commissioner conveyed greetings to President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on behalf of Australia's Governor-General, Ms Sam Mostyn AC, and handed over a formal greeting letter to him.
The president sincerely thanked the governor-general of Australia for the greetings.
The president sought Australia's cooperation to diversify Bangladesh's energy sources and creating opportunities for LNG imports from Australia.
He called for more Australian investment in infrastructure, renewable energy, energy exploration, agro-processing, medical technology, logistics and manufacturing sectors.
The president hoped that the Senior Officials' Meeting and the TIFA meeting scheduled to be held in Canberra next November would play an important role in expanding trade and investment between the two countries.
Mirza Fakhrul Islam welcomed the opportunities in Australia for migration of skills professionals, particularly in the fields of information technology, engineering and other technical areas.
Besides, he sought Australia's continued support in scholarship and academic exchange programmes, as well as support for establishing a campus of the University of Canberra in Dhaka.
He also proposed expanding cooperation between Bangladesh's Technical Training Centres (TTCs) and Australia's Technical and Further Education (TAFE) institutions to develop job-oriented skilled manpower in Bangladesh. In this regard, he emphasised various technical training programmes including caregiver training.
Referring to the Rohingya crisis, the president expressed gratitude to Australia for its continued humanitarian assistance in addressing this crisis and called for Australia's continued cooperation in finding a sustainable solution of the problem.
He expressed hope that the Bangladesh-Australia partnership would place greater emphasis in the future on tangible economic opportunities, skill development, investment and increased connectivity and mobility between the peoples of the two countries.
During the meeting, the high commissioner highlighted the country’s foreign exchange reserves in banks, tax reforms, judicial independence and a positive regulatory environment in relation to Australian business investment here.
She also appreciated banking reforms in Bangladesh and expressed her country's interest in further strengthening Bangladesh-Australia cooperation in various areas of mutual interest.
President's Military Secretary, Secretary, Press Secretary and an Additional Secretary of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs were present during the meeting.

item.title: Muktadir: Overlapping projects across ministries hinder productivity
item.description:
Industries Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir on Thursday said eliminating overlapping projects run by different ministries could ensure double-digit efficiency gains as the government moves to review such duplication to boost national productivity.
Speaking at an event organised by the Ministry of Industries in Motijheel, he said efforts are underway to examine whether projects implemented by different ministries overlap.
“No issue today is confined to one country; we have to look at the whole world,” the minister said, adding that it is not possible to remain outside the existing global system even if one wishes to.
“So, there is no alternative to raising productivity. The nation that increases productivity will be the one that advances,” he said.
Pointing to the ready-made garment (RMG) sector, Muktadir said it has demonstrated how progress can be achieved even with workers from marginalised sections of society.
Speaking at the event, Centre for Policy Dialogue (CPD) Executive Director Nazneen Ahmed said small enterprises need support to grow into medium-sized ones, and that the government coordinates with various sectors to facilitate such growth.
She stressed the need to examine whether these initiatives involve duplication.
Nazneen said the government needs assistance in designing productivity training, adding that replacing people with machines should not be the goal.
Instead, she said, attention should be given to how machinery and technology can enhance workers’ skills, while innovation also needs to be increased.
The CPD executive director noted that women’s participation in large industries is declining.
“Women cannot take the skills training required for automation because of household pressures, so they are falling behind in skill-based jobs,” she said.
She also proposed a refinancing scheme for the SME sector, saying linking loans to productivity improvement could lead to significant growth in the sector.

item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Thursday inaugurated the Tk1,542.16-crore Muhuri-Kohua Flood Control, Drainage and Irrigation Project rehabilitation (Phase I) at Feni aiming to strengthen flood protection, drainage and irrigation facilities in the district.
The prime minister inaugurated the project at around 2.17 pm on Thursday at the Kheyaghat Ghat-Muhuri Bridge area in Parshuram upazila and later exchanged greetings with local people at the venue.
The Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC) approved the project on June 16 at an estimated cost of Tk1,542.16 crore.
Under the project, 67.92 kilometers of flood-control embankments will be rehabilitated, 11.73 kilometers of riverbanks protected and 83.50 kilometers of rivers and water bodies re-excavated.
Besides, 27 irrigation structures will be rehabilitated and 77 inlets will be constructed under the project, which is scheduled to be completed by 2030.
In its next phase, there are plans to construct new embankments along the Muhuri and Kohua rivers and undertake embankment construction, excavation and rehabilitation works along the Silonia River.
Environment, Forest and Climate change Minister and Feni-3 Lawmaker Abdul Awal Mintoo, Water Resources Minister Shahiduddin Chowdhury Anee, State Minister for Water Resources Forhad Hossain Azad, Feni-1 Lawmaker Munshi Rafiqul Alam, Feni-2 Lwmaker Joynal Abdin, Lawmaker Rahana Akter Ranu, among other, were present on the occasion.
Earlier, the prime minister arrived in Feni at around 1:15pm on his daylong tour to attend a series of programs.
After inaugurating the Muhuri-Kohua project in Parshuram, he is scheduled to travel to Fulgazi, where he will join a tree-planting program at Begum Khaleda Zia Women’s College.
He will later visit the Fulgazi District Council Dak Bungalow, where he will inaugurate the supply of electricity to the national grid from the rooftop solar power system installed at the facility.
The prime minister will then rest and offer prayers at the Dak Bungalow. Later in the afternoon, he will attend a program at Fulgazi Government Pilot High School ground, where he will distribute Family Cards and Farmer Cards and provide honorariums to mosque imams, muezzins, khadims and priests.
He is also scheduled to address a public gathering at the venue before returning to Dhaka in the evening.
Under a government initiative, solar systems with a combined capacity of 962.5 kilowatts have been installed on government buildings in Fulgazi, Parshuram and Chhagalnaiya upazilas, including 415 kilowatts in Chhagalnaiya, 298 kilowatts in Parshuram and 249 kilowatts in Fulgazi.
A total of 510 people in Fulgazi are set to receive Family Cards, while 7,643 people across Feni district will receive Farmer Cards.
Honorariums will also be provided to 238 imams, muezzins, khadims and priests in Fulgazi.
Tarique Rahman’s maternal grandfather Easkandar Majumder’s ancestral home is in Sreepur village of Fulgazi upazila in Feni.
Feni-1 constituency also has a longstanding association with his mother, former Prime Minister Begum Khaleda Zia, who was elected from the constituency several times since 1991.

item.description:
Finance Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury on Thursday said transactions through Bangla QR codes will be completely free of charge as the government moves to build a cashless Bangladesh and a digital economy.
"There will be no fee or charge for transactions through Bangla QR. Any transaction made through the QR code will be completely free, with no additional cost," he said.
The minister made the remarks while inaugurating shopping through Bangla QR codes and inspecting QR-based transactions at Banani Kitchen Market in the capital.
Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury said the government would bring people from all sections of society, including Fuchka vendors, rickshaw pullers and small traders, under QR code-based digital financial services.
Under the initiative, ordinary people, roadside vendors and small businesses will be able to receive payments easily through QR codes linked to accounts with any bank or service provider, he said.
"This will eliminate the need to carry cash and make transactions easier and faster," the finance minister said.
He acknowledged that some minor technical challenges or temporary problems might arise at the initial stage, but expressed confidence that those could be resolved quickly.
Cashless transactions have already proved to be convenient and secure in many developed and rapidly growing economies around the world, he said.
"Bangladesh Bank is working to make this international practice universal in Bangladesh," he added.
The finance minister also urged citizens, businesses and service providers to participate in the government initiative to build a cashless and secure economy without hesitation.

item.title: BRUR expels 11, including 3 teachers, over Shaheed Abu Sayed killing
item.description:
Begum Rokeya University, Rangpur (BRUR) has permanently expelled 11 individuals, including three faculty members and eight officials and staff, over their involvement in the killing of student Abu Sayed during the 2024 Anti-Discrimination Student Movement.
The punitive measure was approved during the 123rd meeting of the BRUR Syndicate, the university’s highest policy-making body, on Wednesday night, Vice-Chancellor Prof Dr Md Showkat Ali confirmed on Thursday afternoon.
The three permanently expelled faculty members are Mashiur Rahman, former associate professor of the Mathematics Department; Asaduzzaman Mandal alias Asad, associate professor of Public Administration; and Shariful Islam, associate professor of Political Science and former proctor.
The expelled employees include former Assistant Registrar Rafiul Hasan Russel, Assistant Registrar Hafijur Rahman alias Tufan, Section Officer Moniruzzaman Palash, Office Assistant-cum-Computer Operator Mahabubar Rahman alias Babu, Security Guard Nur Alam Mia, and MLSS staff members Mohammad Nurunnabi Mandal and AKM Amir Hossain, alongside an 11th individual confirmed by university administration.
BRUR Registrar Prof Dr Md Ferdous Rahman said administrative procedures are underway to execute the Syndicate's order. Terming Abu Sayed’s death a momentous and painful chapter in the university's history, VC Prof. Shawkat Ali reaffirmed that disciplinary actions were taken strictly in accordance with university statutes following an internal probe.
Abu Sayed, a key coordinator of the quota reform movement and a student of the English Department, was shot dead by police on July 16, 2024, near the university's main gate. Footage of Sayed standing unarmed with outstretched arms, facing police gunfire, went viral, sparking nationwide protests that ultimately led to the fall of the Sheikh Hasina-led government.

item.title: Govt moves on Teesta Master Plan, feasibility study proposed
item.description:
The government has taken a fresh step toward advancing the much-discussed Teesta Master Plan, with the Ministry of Water Resources sending a Tk 23-crore proposal to the Planning Commission for a feasibility study on the project.
If approved, an international consultant will be appointed through competitive bidding to assess the technical and economic viability of the proposed interventions, including a new barrage, river training, dredging, flood control, water conservation and related infrastructure.
Water Resources Secretary Dr AKM Shahabuddin said the feasibility study would be crucial for taking the Teesta Master Plan toward implementation.
“The technical and economic viability of every component will be assessed through the study, and subsequent works for the main project will be taken based on its recommendations,” he said.
Planning Division Secretary SM Shakil Akhter said the proposal would be examined under the established procedure, taking into account the project's necessity, cost, potential benefits and feasibility.
“If approved, it will pave the way for appointing a consultant through international competitive bidding,” he told BSS.
The government has identified finding a permanent solution to the Teesta River’s problems and promoting economic transformation in the northwestern region as priorities. The BNP's 2026 election manifesto also pledged to ensure a fair share of water from the Teesta and other trans-boundary rivers, while stressing balanced regional development and greater use of the agricultural and economic potential of northern Bangladesh.
The proposed master plan envisages a broad package of river and regional development measures rather than focusing solely on a barrage.
It includes riverbank protection or river training along about 110 kilometres, dredging of another 110 kilometres of the river, and construction of 224 kilometres of flood-control embankments with roads on top.
The plan also proposes constructing or repairing 67 spurs and reclaiming and developing about 170 square kilometres of land.
Engineer Md Ruhul Amin, director general of the Bangladesh Water Development Board (BWDB), said the plan takes an integrated approach covering river-flow management, bank protection, flood control, irrigation and transport infrastructure.
The feasibility study, he said, would determine the precise locations and scope of the proposed works.
The proposed embankment-cum-road infrastructure could improve connectivity in riverside communities that are frequently cut off during the monsoon. At the same time, the embankments would provide flood protection, potentially combining two important infrastructure functions.
Dredging, however, would require careful consideration of the river’s natural behaviour. River expert Mohammad Ejaz said dredging should take into account sediment transport, water discharge and the river’s flow dynamics.
“Merely deepening the riverbed will not provide a long-term solution,” he told the national news agency adding that the feasibility study should identify appropriate dredging locations and determine how dredged sediment would be managed.
A new barrage is another major component under consideration. The government is examining the technical and financial feasibility of constructing another barrage on the Teesta to conserve water during the dry season.
According to Dr Md Ataur Rahman, a professor of Water Resources Engineering at BUET, the feasibility assessment must examine upstream and downstream flows, flood management, irrigation requirements, structural safety, maintenance and environmental considerations alongside water-storage capacity.
The Teesta is closely tied to the lives and economies of people in Rangpur, Lalmonirhat, Nilphamari, Kurigram and Gaibandha. Reduced dry-season flow affects irrigation and agriculture, while high monsoon flows contribute to flooding and river erosion, threatening homes and farmland.
Riverbank protection is therefore another key element of the plan, alongside proposals to strengthen river training and repair or construct spurs. The proposed land reclamation could also open opportunities for agriculture, infrastructure and other forms of local economic development.
Yet the scale of the eventual benefits will depend on the findings of the feasibility study, environmental assessments, final project design, financing, implementation quality and long-term maintenance.
For people in the northern region, the latest move comes after years of surveys, plans and expectations surrounding the Teesta. The proposed feasibility study does not mark the completion of the master plan, but it could move the initiative into a more concrete administrative and technical phase.
Several steps would still remain, including completion of the feasibility study and environmental assessment, finalisation of the project design, government approval, financing and field-level implementation.
If implemented, the Teesta Master Plan would extend beyond a conventional barrage or river-management project. It could bring water conservation, irrigation, flood control, erosion prevention, river training, transport, land management and regional economic development under a single integrated framework.

item.title: City scandal risks damage to Premier League's booming brand
item.description:
The Premier League has won a lengthy legal battle with Manchester City over financial impropriety, but the consequences could leave lasting damage for a league that has long since become the envy of world football.
City face severe sanctions after being found guilty of over 100 charges between 2009 and 2018, with an independent commission exposing "sham" contracts to artificially inflate the club's revenues and reduce costs by more than £900 million ($1.2 billion).
A hefty points deduction resulting in relegation, stripped titles and even expulsion from the English top flight have been mooted as potential sanctions.
But the damage may not be limited to City alone with an entire era of the Premier League now under a cloud.
A takeover in 2008 by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al-Nahyan, the vice-president and deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates, transformed City's fortunes, but also the face of the Premier League.
The club's first top-flight league title for 44 years was one of the most iconic moments in Premier League history when Sergio Aguero netted the winner against QPR in the 94th minute to deny Manchester United the title.
Some of City's rivals have been quick to revel in their downfall.
"Another Premier League medal to be added to the cabinet," posted former Manchester United defender Rio Ferdinand, who was part of the United team that finished second to City in the 2011/12 season.
Yet there could be more lingering collective consequences for a league that has become accustomed to flexing its financial muscle to hoover up the best talent from around the globe.
Italy's Serie A once enjoyed that status in the 1990s.
Although it had lost some of its lustre by the time the Calciopoli scandal came about in 2006, Italian football has arguably never fully recovered in the two decades since.
That case surrounded club officials influencing which referees would officiate their games and led to Juventus being stripped of two titles and relegated to Serie B.
- Haaland exit inevitable?
The question is now whether fans will be turned away from the Premier League after feeling cheated over what they have witnessed over the past 18 years.
In total City have won eight titles in the last 15 seasons.
They rewrote the record books, becoming the first side to ever achieve 100 points and win the English top flight for four consecutive years.
All of those achievements are now labelled with an asterisk.
"If I was a player, I'd be 100 percent sticking those medals in the bin. Of course you would, it's cheating," said former Manchester United captain Roy Keane.
Despite the Premier League's spending power, English clubs have still struggled to keep the world's biggest superstars away from Real Madrid, Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain.
City's demise could also see the Premier League lose its marquee player in Erling Haaland.
"The Premier League is Britain's greatest soft power cultural asset," Simon Chadwick, professor of Afro-Eurasian sport, told AFP. "What happens when people start to question, 'what have I been watching all these years?'"
By contrast, the Premier League has argued the City case is proof of strong governance.
The league pursued and persisted with an investigation which began in 2018 despite City's best attempts to frustrate the process.
"This disciplinary case, and this decision, are the most significant in Premier League history," said the league's chief executive Richard Masters.
"It is a key responsibility of the Premier League to ensure that the rules, approved by the clubs themselves, are upheld to protect the integrity of the competition.
"It is paramount that the league remains competitive and fair for all clubs and for the fans. We take that role extremely seriously."

item.title: Asian Games: Mustafizur’s costly over ends Bangladesh’s gold hopes
item.description:
Bangladesh’s hopes of winning the men’s cricket gold medal at the Asian Games ended on Thursday after Pakistan beat them by six wickets in a rain-shortened semifinal.
Bangladesh made 111 for seven in 13 overs after being sent in, but Pakistan chased down the target with nine balls to spare, reaching 112 for four in 11.3 overs.
The match was still evenly poised when Pakistan needed 36 runs from the last four overs with four wickets in hand.
But Mustafizur Rahman’s second over changed the game. The left-arm pacer conceded 23 runs, including five boundaries, leaving Pakistan needing only 13 from the final three overs.
Abdul Samad struck an unbeaten 30 off 15 balls and Hasan Nawaz made 27 not out off 22 as Pakistan completed the chase comfortably.
Bangladesh had made a strong start with the ball, reducing Pakistan to 17 for two in two overs. Mehidi Hasan removed Sahibzada Farhan before Nasum Ahmed dismissed Maz Sadaqat.
Saim Ayub then added 21 off 12 balls before Mustafizur had him caught off the final delivery of his first over. Mustafizur finished with one wicket but conceded 41 runs in his two overs.
Rishad Hossain and Mehidi took one wicket each for Bangladesh.
Earlier, Towhid Hridoy top-scored for Bangladesh with 42 off 25 balls, hitting four sixes and two fours. He came to the crease after Bangladesh had slipped to 21 for three.
Saif Hasan made 19 off 17 balls and Mosaddek Hossain scored 11, while Mehidi remained unbeaten on eight from four balls.
Sufiyan Muqeem took three wickets for 26 runs for Pakistan.
Bangladesh will play for the bronze medal on Sunday against the loser of Thursday’s second semifinal between India and Sri Lanka.
